hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger is small: template-svc-1 was restarted by a failed liveness probe at 16:10:28 (#1092), dropping capacity to 3/4; it was ready again at 16:11:16 (#1129). Right after, notification-svc began getting 503s from template-svc /render (#1137) and retried immediately with backoff disabled (#1137, #1164, #1205, 0ms delay, up to 4 attempts). Those retries multiplied the load: template-svc hit 590 in-flight requests (3.2x normal, #1187) and then 827 at 4.1x baseline (#1234), and it began load-shedding with 503s (#1212, #1401, #1504). Notification-svc exhausted retries and api-gateway returned 503s to clients (#1186, #1300, #1356, #1474). The fault is not recovering because the retry loop keeps the template-svc queue saturated. The notif-db, redis and notif-worker logs look healthy. The status-poller timeouts against legacy-inventory (#299, #353, ... #1513) are a separate, deprecated healthcheck and do not sit on the notify path, so they are a red herring.

Alternative reading: template-svc itself ran out of request capacity (instance restart at 3/4 capacity, in-flight pool at 590 then 827 with queue-full rejections). If the restart was the cause of the capacity loss, this would be a resource limit rather than amplification. The logs show no memory or GC issue (GC pauses are 6-25ms, heap 30-45%), which weakens this reading.

verdict.recommendedAction: 1) Enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry cap on notification-svc's TemplateClient.render. Immediate retries with backoff disabled are what amplify the load. 2) Shed or pause the excess notify traffic, or temporarily raise template-svc capacity or replicas, so the in-flight queue can drain. 3) Investigate why template-svc-1's liveness probe failed at 16:10:28. 4) Separately, the status-poller healthcheck against deprecated legacy-inventory is timing out. Remove or repoint it so it stops adding noise.

hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger is small: template-svc-1 was restarted by a failed liveness probe at 16:10:28 (#1092), dropping capacity to 3/4; it was ready again at 16:11:16 (#1129). Right after, notification-svc began getting 503s from template-svc /render (#1137) and retried immediately with backoff disabled (#1137, #1164, #1205, 0ms delay, up to 4 attempts). Those retries multiplied the load: template-svc hit 590 in-flight requests (3.2x normal, #1187) and then 827 at 4.1x baseline (#1234), and it began load-shedding with 503s (#1212, #1401, #1504). Notification-svc exhausted retries and api-gateway returned 503s to clients (#1186, #1300, #1356, #1474). The fault is not recovering because the retry loop keeps the template-svc queue saturated. The notif-db, redis and notif-worker logs look healthy. The status-poller timeouts against legacy-inventory (#299, #353, ... #1513) are a separate, deprecated healthcheck and do not sit on the notify path, so they are a red herring.

Alternative reading: template-svc itself ran out of request capacity (instance restart at 3/4 capacity, in-flight pool at 590 then 827 with queue-full rejections). If the restart was the cause of the capacity loss, this would be a resource limit rather than amplification. The logs show no memory or GC issue (GC pauses are 6-25ms, heap 30-45%), which weakens this reading.

input.recommendedAction: 1) Enable exponential backoff with jitter and a retry cap on notification-svc's TemplateClient.render. Immediate retries with backoff disabled are what amplify the load. 2) Shed or pause the excess notify traffic, or temporarily raise template-svc capacity or replicas, so the in-flight queue can drain. 3) Investigate why template-svc-1's liveness probe failed at 16:10:28. 4) Separately, the status-poller healthcheck against deprecated legacy-inventory is timing out. Remove or repoint it so it stops adding noise.
